Section 2—Hazard(s) identification
Section 3—Composition and information on ingredients

Section 10—Stability and reactivity
Section 11—Toxicological information
Section 12—Ecological information
Section 13—Disposal considerations
Section 14—Transport information
Section 15—Regulatory information
Section 16—Any other relevant information

questions.question: What are five (5) safe manual handling procedures to observe when using trolleys?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, five of the following:
Assess the route you will take when using trolleys. Identify and manage any hazards that may be present on the route.
Consider how you will negotiate doorways, corners and changes in level.
Check the trolley to ensure it is in operational order and free from damage or faults – always check wheels.
Do not overstack the trolley.
Ensure you can see clearly over the trolley load.
Ensure the weight is distributed evenly on the trolley.
Push the trolley. Avoid pulling.
Engage breaks when stationary.
Avoid loose or rough surfaces.
If the trolley is faulty, isolate the trolley to avoid use by other staff members.
Attach signage to the trolley (Out of Order).
Complete an Equipment Maintenance Report and submit to Department Manager ASAP.

questions.question: What are three (3) safe manual handling techniques to observe when lifting?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Use team lifts when lifting heavy or awkward items.
Don’t lift weights above 16-20kg when standing.
All weights over 55kgs should be lifted with mechanical assistance or using a team lift.
Use technology or equipment to help with lifting heavy or awkward items.
Apply correct lifting procedures – feet close together; brace before taking the load; bend the knees; lift with the legs, not the back; keep load close to body.
Do not lift with the back.

questions.question: What are four (4) ways housekeeping attendants can support disposing of waste responsibly?
guidance: Answer may address but is not limited to four of the following:
Separate recyclable and non-recyclable waste.
Place recyclable items such as newspapers, magazines, dry food packaging, cardboard boxes and empty drink containers in designated recycling bins.
Place compostable material in a designated bin if the establishment has an organic waste program or your local government collects organic waste.
Identify hazardous items such as batteries and separate them into designated areas so they can be disposed of in accordance with local regulations (they must not be put in with general waste).
Separate chemical waste and store in designated store rea for collection by registered chemical disposal company.

questions.question: What are six (6) safe storage procedures for hazardous cleaning products?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, four of the following:
Label all hazardous cleaning products clearly and appropriately, including the product name, hazard warnings, and usage instructions.
Store separately from other cleaning products in a designated storage area. This area should be clearly marked with a warning sign and locked to prevent unauthorised access.
Store in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated area.
Use appropriate storage containers that are compatible with the hazardous cleaning products being stored. Ensure that the containers are tightly sealed to prevent leaks or spills.
Store away from heat sources, electrical equipment, and flames.
Ensure that the storage areas have appropriate fire safety equipment, such as fire extinguishers.
Ensure hazardous cleaning products are easily accessible to staff who need to use them for cleaning tasks. However, ensure that only trained and authorised personnel can access these products.
All staff undertake training on the handling, storage, and disposal of hazardous cleaning products.

questions.question: What are three (3) procedures for cleaning mirrors and glassware?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Wipe over with microfibre cloth to remove dust.
Spray solution of vinegar and water or glass cleaner onto the mirror or glass surface, making sure to cover the entire surface.
Use a clean, dry microfiber cloth to wipe the glass surface in a circular motion, starting from the top and working your way down.
For larger surfaces such as windows, remove any excess water or cleaning solution with a squeegee. Start at the top of the glass and pull the squeegee down, wiping the blade clean after each pass.
Use a dry cloth to wipe any remaining streaks or water droplets from the glass surface.

Dispose of used PPE.
Wash and sanitise hands.
